speaker: M. D. Kruskal (catalogue: V. S. Kruskal)
title: Surreal numbers: arithmetic, exponentiation and asymptotics
summary: The manuscript names only \ru{Крускал}; the catalogue's initials V.~S. are retained as a discrepant authority field. Identification with Martin David Kruskal is a strong contextual inference: the subject and construction agree with the work explicitly attributed to M.~D.~Kruskal by \citet[Introduction and Chap.~10]{gonshor1986surreal}. The lecture begins with Conway's book and Knuth's mathematical novel (\citet{knuth1974surreal}), then constructs surreal numbers by ordinal sign sequences, orders them, defines arithmetic by simplest cuts, and explains infinite numbers, infinitesimals and natural ordinal arithmetic. The final page sketches exponentiation and proposes asymptotic integration as an application. Basic arithmetic is exposition; the exponential construction belongs to the subsequently published Kruskal--Gonshor development. The Gaussian formula and integer criterion require mathematical emendation. The entries 1977-445.1--4 in the supplied previous index describe the same opening material: these are overlapping-source aliases, not evidence of another earlier lecture. The next dated heading, Polyakov on 13 November, begins on P000791; the catalogue's overlapping page range must not be read as a talk boundary.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Nonabelian Toda chains, loop-space gauge fields, and a proposed area law
summary: The lecture begins on P000791, after the preceding meeting’s material, and ends on P000798. Its first part passes from a lattice principal chiral model to the matrix Toda chain, a difference-operator Lax equation, formal transfer matrices, and conserved coefficients. The second part treats lattice curvature and holonomy as a route to a chiral-field description of Yang--Mills fields on loop space. A functional flatness equation, conservation equation, prospective higher currents, and a spectral linear problem are written, but the measure in the proposed loop-space action is expressly left undefined. The final part seeks a string analogue of the Klein--Gordon Green function and an area-law asymptotic, then reduces the contour dependence to its six projected areas in four dimensions. The proposed self-dual area expression must be distinguished from the minimum area of an arbitrary spanning surface.\par The matrix Toda discussion was subsequently developed by Krichever and others; a modern primary survey explicitly attributes its unpublished origin to Polyakov \citep[\S1, equation (1.3), and \S9]{takebezabrodin2025multicomponent}. Polyakov’s 1979 publication identifies the loop-space programme, but the available author-hosted publication record verifies its abstract and chronology, not every formula in this notebook \citep[abstract]{polyakov1979string}. The projected-area proposal therefore receives a mathematical audit instead of being silently promoted to a general Plateau theorem.

speaker: A. S. Schwarz
title: Gauge quotients, instanton determinants, and the sigma-model Coulomb gas
summary: The meeting begins on P000799 with palindromes and Krichever’s isolated phrase about instantons without bundles; neither supplies an additional developed argument. Schwarz explains regularized functional integrals, gauge degeneracy, the Faddeev--Popov prescription, and its finite-dimensional quotient-measure analogue. He then describes the semiclassical contribution of rational-map instantons in the two-dimensional sphere-valued sigma model. The key calculation replaces a difficult determinant by its metric variation, separates local heat coefficients from zero modes, and cancels the latter against the Gram determinant on instanton moduli. Its final zeros-and-poles measure becomes a two-component Coulomb gas and, at the indicated coupling, a free-fermion calculation.\par Most of the method is identifiable in work already circulating before this meeting. The detailed 1979 Fateev--Frolov--Schwarz paper says that its central measure formula had been sketched in Frolov and Schwarz’s 1978 announcement \citep[\S1, equation (1.9), and reference 13]{fateevfrolovschwarz1979quantum}. The notebook’s missing zero-mode exclusions, determinant sign, and dropped heat derivative are recorded as faithful mathematical errors. The resulting one-loop instanton-sector calculation is not a proof of the full interacting continuum field theory.

speaker: V. E. Zakharov; L. N. Lipatov
title: A variational principle for rational zero-curvature systems; large-order perturbation theory
summary: The catalogue names Zakharov, but the dated page P000804 first announces Lev Nikolaevich Lipatov, and P000806 explicitly changes speaker to Lipatov. Both contributions belong to this meeting. Zakharov expands a rational zero-curvature equation with disjoint simple poles, conjugates its residues to prescribed Jordan forms, and supplies an action in those orbit variables. The conservation-law remark and a conjecture about multiple Hamiltonian structures follow. The corresponding Zakharov--Mikhailov paper was received on 3 October 1978 and published in 1980; receipt proves the existence of an earlier manuscript, but is not by itself evidence of public circulation before this lecture \citep[equations (1)--(10) and receipt line]{zakharovmikhailov1980variational}.\par Lipatov explicitly cites his 1977 paper. He motivates the asymptotics of perturbative coefficients through renormalized scalar field theory, invariant charge, and the Landau leading-logarithm formula, then explains the saddle-point method and its sharp four-dimensional Sobolev profile \citep[\S\S2--4]{lipatov1977divergence}. His portion is therefore primarily exposition of prior work. The notebook’s claimed infinite limit of the displayed running coupling contradicts its own positive denominator. A final, separately attributed Zakharov intervention connects the critical cubic equation with Yang--Mills equations without recording the required ansatz.

speaker: Alain Guichardet
title: Extensions of representations and first cohomology
summary: Guichardet starts with extensions split as underlying abelian groups and the cocycle construction of their first cohomology classes. He then treats Lie-algebra extensions, separation by infinitesimal characters, and the relative cohomology describing extensions split over a subalgebra. The topological setting introduces a substantive choice of category: continuous representations, smooth vectors, and Harish--Chandra modules need not have identical extension groups. The notes distinguish ordinary cohomology from the quotient by the closure of coboundaries through the affine-group example, and mention the established semisimple classification. The meeting ends on P000811 immediately after introducing dual orbits for a semidirect product; no extension theorem for those orbits is recorded.\par Delorme’s 1977 paper supplies a checked primary source for the continuous unitary cohomology statements \citep[\S0(a), \S V(C), \S V(D)]{delorme1977cohomologie}. Guichardet’s related article appeared in 1979, but a contemporary primary bibliography lists a June 1978 preprint; its later publication date alone cannot establish that this lecture contained a new theorem \citep[reference 20]{charfi1980extensions}. Several compressed statements on P000811 lack the representations or category needed to identify a theorem and are retained as unresolved identifications.

title: Calendar-year divider: 1979
summary: This is a catalogue divider, \emph{YEAR 1979}, rather than a separate lecture. Its linked page range overlaps the conclusion of Guichardet's December lecture and the reading programme and Belavin material beginning with the dated heading 12 February 1979 on P000812. No independent mathematical occurrence is created from the divider. In particular, the earlier index's 1977-451.1--13 must not be interpreted as a talk by this record: those titles describe the overlapping Guichardet and Belavin pages. The actual occurrences are reassigned by the handwritten headings in the present chapter. The catalogue is verified at \citet{mccme2026gelfand}; its grouping is retained as provenance, not taken as evidence of authorship.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand (catalogue attribution; reading list credited to A. A. Belavin)
title: A reading programme for the physics discussions
summary: The heading \ru{Что нужно знать? (по А. А. Белавину)} introduces a reading programme: Feynman's lectures, statistical physics and path integrals; Huang on Onsager's solution; Klein on nineteenth-century mathematics; Dirac on monopoles, quantum mechanics and relativity; Akhiezer--Berestetskii; Yang--Mills; and Konopleva--Popov. The catalogue attributes the record to I.~M. Gelfand, but the page explicitly credits Belavin for the programme. No mathematical assertion is manufactured from this bibliography. The separate underlined \ru{Белавин} introduces record 453 on the same page. The notebook's Feynman coauthor \ru{Гиббсом} refers to Hibbs, not Gibbs; the identification is independently supported by the emended edition's editor \citep{feynmanhibbs1965path}.

speaker: A. A. Belavin
title: Instanton matrices, lattice fermions and factorized scattering
summary: An instanton parametrization challenge precedes the main exposition of exactly solvable two-dimensional quantum field theories. The talk connects the finite XYZ chain with lattice fermions, the massive Thirring and sine-Gordon models, and Zamolodchikov's exchange algebra. Baxter's elliptic weights and commuting transfer matrices organize the hidden symmetries. Several displayed formulas have normalization or spectral-origin errors, while the suggestion that gauge averaging alone proves confinement overstates its conclusion. The ADHM paragraph and beginning of the gauge argument already appear in the supplied prior index as 1977-451.11--13; their source is this same dated page, so this is a provenance duplication, not an earlier historical occurrence.

speaker: A. A. Belavin
title: Exchange algebras, transfer matrices and the spin-1 question
summary: The continuation develops the Yang--Baxter consistency condition, commuting transfer matrices, the eight-vertex ansatz and monodromy multiplication. It asks for anisotropic parameters in a displayed spin-one Hamiltonian and ends with an unfinished Ising transfer-matrix assertion. Literal errors matter: the sample functional equation is incompatible with the stated regularity unless its elliptic weight vanishes, and the spin-one density fails a necessary regular difference-form Yang--Baxter condition under the commutator normalization explicitly given on P000819. The later Fateev--Zamolodchikov model supplies a nearby correctly normalized construction; it is not a solution of the printed density. The chapter's separately marked algebraic audit makes that distinction testable.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand, reporting a lecture by Yu. I. Manin
title: Complex Minkowski space and the full Yang-Mills ambitwistor correspondence
summary: S.~I. Gelfand reports Manin's explanation of the 1978 Witten and Isenberg--Yasskin--Green construction for general Yang--Mills fields, without a self-duality assumption. The geometry passes from the Grassmannian and real null twistors to bundles on the incidence quadric and their third formal neighbourhood. The notebook's conformal stabilizer, group equality and Yang--Mills commutator sign require correction. Beilinson's separate intervention begins on P000823 and supplies the missing triviality condition on the quadrics of null directions. The broad catalogue range must not absorb Fuchs's separately dated lecture beginning on P000824.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: The complete-flag explanation of the ambitwistor transform
summary: Beilinson explains the preceding construction by the complete-flag double fibration: pull a connection from the Grassmannian to the correspondence space, take horizontal sections along null curves, and descend to the incidence quadric. The final line explicitly requires triviality on \(\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1\). This is an explanation of the 1978 full-connection ambitwistor correspondence, not the unrelated derived-category theorem bearing Beilinson's name. The supplied prior index places this same page under 1977-457.1--3; these are source aliases, not an earlier seminar occurrence. P000824 begins the separately dated Fuchs lecture. The page itself has no new date: 26 February 1979 is the catalogue date and is consistent with its position immediately after the dated S.~I. Gelfand report.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Graded Lie algebras: a partially supplied lecture omitted from the record list
summary: The dated heading \ru{5/III-79, Д. Б. Фукс} on P000824 establishes a separate lecture between Beilinson and Ogievetsky. It is omitted from the supplied fourteen-record list and is added here explicitly to avoid suppressing mathematics present in the attached corpus. P000824--P000825 cover transitivity, Cartan vector-field families and prolongation; P000829 resumes with twisted loops and a period-three bracket. P000826--P000828 are not supplied, so this is not a complete account of the lecture. The same available segments were previously placed under 1977-457.4--7 and 1977-457.17--19, although their visible date is March 1979. The prior index's 1977-457.1--3 instead describe Beilinson's P000823, and 1977-457.20--25 describe Ogievetsky's P000830--P000831. These are provenance aliases, not historical recurrences.

speaker: V. I. Ogievetskii
title: Supersymmetry algebra, superspace, and chiral fields
summary: Although headed \ru{Супергравитация}, the surviving talk develops the kinematics of flat four-dimensional supersymmetry: the super-Poincar\'e brackets, the spinor description of Lorentz vectors, odd coordinates, superfields, supertranslations, and chiral coordinates. It contains no gravitational action, local supersymmetry constraints, or quantum-finiteness theorem. The first two pages overlap items 1977-457.20--25 in the supplied previous index; the dated heading on P000830 shows that these are duplicate indexing of the same manuscript material, not evidence of an earlier seminar occurrence. The substantive continuation on P000832--P000833 supplies the transformation and chirality formulas. P000829 belongs to the preceding Fuchs material, and P000834 begins Lebedev. Most of this introduction was already printed in the speaker's 1975 review, whose English translation carries a 1976 copyright \citep[Secs.~2--3]{ogievetskymezincescu1975superfields}.

speaker: D. R. Lebedev
title: Local Lie algebras and formal differential groups
summary: The dated heading is \ru{Лебедев (Митя). О результатах Ритта и Кириллова по дифференциальной алгебре}. Three strands are juxtaposed: continuous support-local brackets on sections of bundles, Kirillov's rank-one classification, and Ritt's formal differential groups with one derivation. A formal pseudodifferential-symbol example connects these to the speaker's Volterra-group work. The source does not justify identifying the smooth, formal and differential-algebraic categories. In particular its ``ten Ritt algebras'' count omits three finite types, and its universal extension assertion omits even the product of two substitution groups. The contact formula also has a genuine sign inconsistency, confirmed from the scan and by two independent calculations. The question marks at higher ranks specify no classification conjecture.

speaker: G. B. Shabat (catalogue); initial in notes uncertain
title: Web geometry and a Zamolodchikov intervention on vertex models
summary:
The first part reports Chern and Griffiths on algebraic webs, abelian relations, the Castelnuovo rank bound and linearization at maximal rank. Gelfand adds Crofton's formula and the hexagonal three-web problem. The notebook cites the exact 1978 Chern--Griffiths article. The main theorem was then believed proved, but the authors' 1981 correction added normality; Tr\'epreau supplied the unrestricted result in a preprint of 4 August 2005, published in 2006. The heading's last year digit and the speaker's initial are uncertain: the catalogue gives 2 April 1979 and G.~B.~Shabat, while the transcription tentatively reads 1978 and K.~Shabat. Catalogue identity is retained with this qualification.\\
The latter part of P000839 explicitly names \ru{Замолодчиков А. (Саша)}. His matrix contractions, three-line move and statistical-mechanical interpretation continue through P000840, without a second date. Their assignment as an intervention in this session is an editorial reconstruction. These are not assertions by Shabat. The general asymptotic assertions lack enough hypotheses to identify a definite theorem. P000841 begins a different dated talk, R.~E.~Kallosh on 24 September 1979, and P000842 continues it; neither page belongs to this record.
